findings.title: Fresh-witness acquisition liveness/circularity for a PRESENT head is neither closed nor named HOLD
findings.statement: K1 current derivation needs two fresh ordered native M2 witnesses against a live TrustedContext.Challenges entry under the current HELD operation (current.go currentNativeWitnesses; proofs.go verifyNativeAt live branch; evidence age <=min(plan,120s)). Producing them requires challenge issuance and observer Engine ExecCreate/Start, which the proposal correctly assigns to K2B. But K2B admission says only 're-verify K1 current where available' (contract section 6) and names a replacement authority solely for ABSENT head (D-PREPUBLICATION/BootstrapPhaseAuthorization). For PRESENT head with expired or missing witnesses there is no named admission authority: either observation is admitted without any defined predicate (hidden missing authority) or it is blocked, in which case no CurrentView can ever be re-obtained once the first 120 s pass (liveness deadlock).
findings.counterexample: Steady state after bootstrap: head PRESENT, readback and HELD lease valid, last M2 observed 121 s ago. DeriveCurrent -> CURRENT_NATIVE_WITNESS_UNKNOWN_MISMATCH_OR_EXPIRED. AuthorizeEffect(observe) -> 'K1 current where available' is unavailable; D-PREPUBLICATION does not apply (head is PRESENT). No rule in contract.md, authority-and-effect-gates.json or the 18 failure examples decides this request.
sourceEvidence: design 8874 acceptance-matrix A36 green (preserved verbatim in future-runtime-A01-A40.json): 'immutable terminal seal plus a fresh common normal:3 operation lease admits later observation/rotation' - an authority the K2B section never carries forward or HOLDs

eb32 trust.go: Challenges map keyed operationId+NUL+C2(scope) => exactly one live challenge per (operation, Node); after an EFFECT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN observation the retry path (replace challenge vs new operation/fence) is unspecified
authority-and-effect-gates.json RootDecisions has 4 entries; none covers PRESENT-head observation admission
findings.missingAuthority: Closed, method-scoped observation/witness-refresh admission (challenge issuance + owned ExecCreate/Start) that is not CurrentView, plus retry/supersession semantics under K1's single challenge slot
findings.requiredRevision: Name the authority (e.g. adopt or reject the 8874 A36 'terminal seal + fresh common normal:3 lease' rule explicitly) or add a fifth Root HOLD decision; state that until decided every effect that needs a CurrentView on a real system is BLOCKED; specify the retry semantics; add red/green failure examples for PRESENT-head-expired-witness and for retry-after-UNKNOWN.

findings.title: TrustedContext.MigrationOperationID is classified as a current-operation field but K1 uses it as a historical plan-level operation selector
findings.statement: producer-matrix P12 places MigrationOperationID under 'ReadCurrent active common-cohort operation registry' with validation 'MigrationOperationID exact current authority-selected ID'. In eb32 it is read only in recipes.go recipeSources as the alias operationId fallback for records whose body has no operationId (successor-plan proofs); proofs.go proofOperationAt then resolves it in History.Operations for historical use and in Operations for live use. K1's own durable two-epoch fixture sets it to the expired epoch-1 operation that is absent from current Operations.
findings.reviewerReproduction: Scratch-only Go test on a git-archive copy of eb32 (never in product): control Verify/Current pass; MigrationOperationID := Current.OperationID (P12 as written) -> Verify and VerifyCurrentProjectionSet both refuse 'proof signed for different current operation' (first failing plan proof path varies with Go map order: scheduleDisabledReadback / expectedInventoryHead/readbackProof / allLaunchSurfaces); facts.migrationOperationId changed alone -> 'plan/body/noOverlap: proof subject differs'. See reviewer-go-scratch-test.log.txt.
findings.impact: A K2A implemented from P12 refuses every valid multi-epoch history (fail-closed but unusable) and would version this field in the current-registry SnapshotToken instead of binding it to the authenticated plan/history archive. It also leaves unstated that TrustedContext.MigrationOperationID and SemanticInputs.facts.migrationOperationId must be the same authenticated plan-level HELD operation (K1 cross-checks them only indirectly via the signed noOverlap subject).
findings.requiredRevision: Move MigrationOperationID to the history/plan producer (P08/P18 family), define it as the plan's original migration operation, require equality with facts.migrationOperationId and existence in HistoricalContext.Operations, and add a failure example.

The contract forbids K2A signers, nonce allocation, publication and Engine exec.

findings.title: Interval-conservative clock use is required but its mechanism against K1's single Now is unspecified
findings.statement: Contract section 4 requires validating the whole uncertainty interval against every bound and then passing the actual UTC observation to K1. K1 evaluates its many internal time predicates (recordUse at<=Now, status <=120s, challenge/lease windows, proof freshness, key intervals) at one Now; K2 cannot validate them over an interval without duplicating K1 logic. The contract must name a sound mechanism (one feasible option: evaluate K1 at both interval endpoints and require both to pass with identical outputs, which is sound only if every K1 time predicate is convex in Now; the reviewer found each inspected eb32 predicate to be a half-line or half-open interval). The bound value and clock source stay Root's D-CLOCK choice; the reviewer chooses neither.

findings.title: Normative refusal names in contract.md are outside the closed errorCatalog
findings.statement: contract.md uses REPLAY_OR_SCOPE_MISMATCH (section 4), NO_CURRENT_HEAD and TRUST_UNKNOWN (section 5); the catalog has LIVE_/HISTORICAL_CHALLENGE_UNKNOWN_OR_REPLAY, NO_CURRENT_HEAD_OR_STALE_CURRENT_SET and TRUST_UNKNOWN_OR_PIN_MISMATCH. The owner validator checks only rows and examples against the catalog.

findings.title: Owner field census is regex-based; future code gates need a go/types census
findings.statement: With the trust.go raw hash re-pinned (as any future K2 change will do), the owner regex census passes an embedded exported field, an embedded *KeyGrant and a Now time.Time->any type change (V01c-V03c PASS); named fields and new named types are caught. At eb32 the exact raw-hash pin makes the census correct, and the reviewer go/types census independently confirms 13 types / 73 fields / 0 embedded. Semantic placement (V06), wrong-but-cataloged refusals (V07), emptied forbidden-effect list (V08) and inverted Root-decision text (V09) also pass: expected static limits, so they must be covered by review and executed tests, not labels.

findings.title: DTO non-forgeability has no named Go enforcement
findings.statement: migrationverify.NewVerifier is exported, takes plain exported structs and is not under internal/; any package can call it with hand-built inputs. Contract section 5 says constructors stay behind K2A but names no mechanism. Require unexported-field authenticated DTOs, an import-boundary test (only the reviewed K2A package imports migrationverify and constructs InstalledTrust/TrustedContext), and that K2B never accepts a K1 Report, derived digest or caller-supplied SnapshotToken as authority (it re-acquires).

findings.title: VerifierPublication is not required to equal the measured running verifier
findings.statement: AST: all five VerifierPublication fields are read only in NewVerifier for format (ID constant, hash shape, non-empty CIRunIDs). P02 authenticates a publication but never requires ArtifactSHA256 to equal the digest of the executable actually running K1/K2 (via the installation receipt and a reviewed self-measurement path), so an authentic publication of artifact X could accompany running binary Y. Combined with K2-I1 (inv-node does not link K1), the future integration entrypoint must be the measured executable.
